study_identification_part.si4_title: Gray matter atrophy is constrained by normal structural brain network architecture in depression

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To investigate the association between gray matter atrophy and normal connectome architecture at individual level in depression.

rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Two independent datasets were included in this study: a discovery dataset and a replication dataset... The discovery dataset included 105 nevertreated first-episode patients with depression and matched 130 healthy controls (HCs) recruited from the first out-patient services of Department of Psychiatry, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University... The replication dataset included 106 patients with depression and matched 126 HCs. The protocol to recruit the replication dataset was approved by the research ethical committee of the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.

nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: ...we trained a Gaussian process regression model to predict regional GMV from age and sex in HCs... Functional connectivity networks were generated by computing pairwise Pearson ' s correlations between the average time series of 246 brain regions followed by Fisher ' z transformation in healthy population (http://www.brainnetome.org/) (Dong et al., 2022; Fan et al., 2016). This brain atlas was chosen for its joint validation using both functional and structural anatomy and connectivity (Fan et al., 2016). Four brain regions were excluded for low SNR (average SNR <100). As a result, we obtained a 242 × 242 × N functional connectivity matrix for healthy group (N was the number of HCs).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: A backfoward stepwise regression analysis was used to identify epicenters. A linear regression was used to evaluate the model performance (R^2). Pearson's correlation was used to correlate disease exposure with atrophy severity (Z-scores). k-means clustering was used to identify subgroups based on the correlation coefficients between structural network and atrophy patterns. Two-sample t-tests were used to compare demographic characteristics between subgroups.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Gray matter atrophy in depression is constrained by the structural brain connectome of multiple disease epicenters with high participation coefficients, and this relationship reveals two subgroups with different ages of onset.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study found that a structural multi-epicenter model best explained individual gray matter atrophy in depression (explaining 44% ± 16% of variance), outperforming single-epicenter and functional connectivity models. Patients had an average of 8.45 epicenters, with significant sharing of hubs like the thalamus, hippocampus, and medial frontal gyrus, which had higher participation coefficients than other regions. Brain regions with stronger structural connections to these epicenters showed greater atrophy (mean R = 0.50 ± 0.12). This connectome-atrophy link was used to identify two distinct patient subgroups that differed significantly in their age of onset (p=0.044).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: 1. Insufficient clinical data to link findings to clinical manifestations. 2. Exclusion of patients with comorbidities limits generalizability. 3. Lack of detailed medication information in the replication dataset prevents analysis of medication effects.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Our study has several limitations. First, we failed to record enough clinical data to deeply investigated whether and how the association between normal connectome architecture and gray matter atrophy underlay the clinical manifestation in depression. Second, only patients without other mental disorders comorbidities were recruited in this study. Future studies could recruit more heterogeneous samples to investigate the effect of comorbidity on these results. Third, in the replication dataset, all patients were taking medicine at the scan and we failed to record detailed information on medicine.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study uses an individualized approach to model brain atrophy, which is a departure from traditional group-level analyses and helps to account for the heterogeneity of depression. The identification of subgroups based on the connectome-atrophy relationship is a notable application.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study provides a novel individualized approach to understanding the neuropathology of depression, linking structural atrophy to the brain's network architecture. A key finding is that a multi-epicenter model based on structural covariance networks, rather than a single epicenter or functional networks, best explains the heterogeneous patterns of gray matter loss. The analysis successfully identified clinically relevant subgroups based on age of onset, highlighting the potential of this method for resolving heterogeneity in depression. The findings were robust, as they were replicated in an independent dataset with medicated patients.
